tasks.title: Class from a field description
tasks.statement: Write make_class(name, fields): using type(...), create a class with the given name, an __init__(self, *values) (the number of values must match the number of fields, otherwise TypeError), and a __repr__ of the form P(x=1, y=2).
tasks.hint: Define init and repr as nested functions and return type(name, (), {"__init__": init, "__repr__": repr_}).

tasks.title: Registry of descendants (__init_subclass__)
tasks.statement: Complete the base class Plugin: every descendant automatically ends up in the dictionary Plugin.registry. The key is the name argument from the class statement (class Json(Plugin, name="json")) or the class name in lowercase.
tasks.hint: def __init_subclass__(cls, name=None, **kwargs): super().__init_subclass__(**kwargs); Plugin.registry[name or cls.__name__.lower()] = cls.

tasks.title: Required attribute of a descendant
tasks.statement: Complete Shape: every descendant must have an integer attribute sides when the class is created; if it is missing or is not an int, raise TypeError right at the moment the class is defined.
tasks.hint: __init_subclass__: if not isinstance(getattr(cls, "sides", None), int): raise TypeError(...).

tasks.title: Singleton via a metaclass
tasks.statement: Write a metaclass Singleton: each class with this metaclass has at most one instance — a repeated call of the class returns the already created one, and __init__ runs only once. Different classes get different instances.
tasks.hint: Keep a dictionary of instances in the metaclass; __call__(cls, *args, **kwargs): if cls is not in the dictionary, create it via super().__call__.

tasks.title: A metaclass collects commands
tasks.statement: Write a metaclass CommandMeta: when a class is created, it collects the functions with the cmd_ prefix into a dictionary commands (the key is the name without the prefix) and puts it into the class. Other attributes stay as they are.
tasks.hint: In __new__: ns["commands"] = {k[4:]: v for k, v in ns.items() if k.startswith("cmd_") and callable(v)}; return super().__new__(mcs, name, bases, ns).

tasks.title: Forbidding inheritance
tasks.statement: Write a metaclass FinalMeta: if any parent of the new class has an attribute __final__ equal to True, creating the class must end with TypeError (such a class cannot be inherited from).
tasks.hint: In __new__: if any(getattr(base, "__final__", False) for base in bases): raise TypeError(...).

tasks.title: Box[int] as a generic type
tasks.statement: Teach the class Box to support the notation Box[int] (and Box[str, int]): the __class_getitem__ method returns a types.GenericAlias with the original class and the arguments.

tasks.title: Forbidding repeated names in a class body
tasks.statement: Write a metaclass NoDupMeta: using __prepare__, it supplies its own namespace (a dict subclass) that raises TypeError if a name (other than special ones starting with two underscores) is defined twice in the class body. The class must otherwise be created in the usual way.
tasks.hint: __prepare__ is a class method of the metaclass: return an instance of a dict subclass with __setitem__; in __new__ pass dict(ns) to super().__new__.

tasks.title: Counting instances per class
tasks.statement: Write a metaclass Counted: every class with this metaclass (and each descendant separately) has an attribute instances — how many instances were created by exactly this class.
tasks.hint: In the metaclass __init__: cls.instances = 0; in __call__: cls.instances += 1; return super().__call__(*args, **kwargs).
